original.description: The increase in small satellite missions has intensified the need for compliance to international space debris de-orbiting requirements. To meet these requirements CubeSat-class missions frequently rely on their primary On-Board Computer (OBC) and Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) to activate disposal mechanisms, however deployment and late-mission failures; such as battery degradation, bus freeze, or cyber compromise; can prevent successful disposal execution.This activity addresses this gap through the development of the Secure Autonomous Disposal Interface and Safety Module: a standardised, independent Disposal Trigger Module (DTM) compatible withCubeSat buses from 1U to 16U across a variety of disposal mechanisms. The DTM shall implement two autonomy levels of increasing complexity and prove resilient to spacecraft failures and cyberattacks. The project targets bring the technology to TRL6.

original.description: This activity investigates concepts for providing on-demand PNT services during crises by leveraging satellite communication systems. It aims to support continuity of positioning, navigation, and timing when terrestrial infrastructures fail due to natural disasters or humanitarian emergencies. The study will identify relevant use cases, define system concepts and requirements, and assess feasibility through preliminary designs. It will also demonstrate key components and functions via small-scale laboratory proof-of-concept setups. The outcome will include a mission study, roadmap, and verification report for future demonstrations. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

original.description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. This study aims at characterising the needs for space-based observations of atmospheric N2O, starting from a user and science perspective. Knowledge gaps are identified related to the N2O production and life cycle, its impact on stratospheric ozone, and its role in the Earth's radiation balance that can be addressed with the help of satellite observations, with a focus on information that can be provided from satellite observations. The study explores the space of requirements that satellite observations of atmospheric N2O (Level-2) and measurements of radiances at the top of the atmosphere (Level-1) would have to meet in order to contribute to addressing these knowledge gaps.

original.description: NAVISP-EL1-117-Resilience Techniques and Algorithms for GNSS Space Receivers in Interference, Jamming and Spoofing Conditions: Thisactivity aims to enhance the resilience of GNSS space receivers against interference, jamming, and spoofing in LEO. It will study and evaluate novel detection and mitigation techniques, including potential spin-in from terrestrial applications. The scope includesdefining standardized threats and scenarios to support future specifications for space receivers. The work involves simulations andearly prototyping of selected technologies to validate concepts. The goal is to maintain GNSS receiver performance during RFI events without monitoring or reporting interference. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

original.description: This procurement covers the provision of Flight Operations Support Services for Copernicus missions operated by ESOC for the period2027-2032. The scope includes the support to all activities required for the preparation and execution of flight operations, such as routine operations, LEOP, commissioning, and end-of-life/deorbiting. It encompasses all key technical disciplines needed to ensuresafe and reliable operations.The service shall ensure continuity with the current contract through a structured phase-in, enabling a progressive ramp-up to full operational readiness. The service shall deliver the agility required to onboard the new Copernicus Expansion missions entrusted to ESOC while maintaining operational support to the Copernicus first generation missions, in line withthe Copernicus Programme framework.
